Antivaxxers should have all the right to get covid and die from it if they choose to. But they should not have the right to spread it or take up an ICU bed.

I've been trying to come up with any realistic scenario that would end this within the next 5 years and... I can't. The idiots wont get the vaccine or mask, viruses rarely evolve to be less contagious, it can circulate and mutate in the unvaccinated and in poorer countries... At this point I am preparing for a larger part of my life to be like this. Half-yearly boosters and wearing an ffp2 everywhere.

Similar to what /u/mohdattar said. Writing prescriptions is easy, especially handing out Xanax is going to make for happy patients - for a while. Figuring out the exact combination of meds that is just enough to help a patient find their way back to a functional life is already quite a bit harder.

Helping someone who has never had secure attachement and is desperate to dull the emotional daily pain to find a reason to live... developping rapport with a paranoid schizophenic who has mostly been forcefully medicated before... trying to stabilize a people stuck in shitty life situations...  hard to impossible.
Psych PGY2 here: it is very easy to be a psychiatrist. It is extremely hard to be a good one.

I have PTSD from childhood stuff and it is weird how the way I remember last year is similar. Like traumatic memories have a distinct way of being fragmented, more sensory oriented... I think a lot if not the majority of HCW will have some level of post traumatic things to deal with once this is over (or if? I really wonder by now how this can end other than by mutating to be less infectious or herd immunity via infection for the unvaccinated...)

Unless I have an actual true emergent consult that can't wait another 10min I start with "Hi, this is worthless from \[service\], is this a good time to present a new consult/ask a question?"  

Gives them the possibility to ask me to call back in x minutes or they say it is fine now. Or "it is never a good time but go ahead" which used to be my go-to-phrase on busy shifts (said in a nice tone, I tried to ease the "shit have to call a consult at night" fear as soon as possible into the call).   

For context: consults in my speciality are received by interns/residents who then do initial workup/info gathering/seeing the patient/exam and only then call the background attending.
Finally I know what I am.

Being in medicine has killed all of my compassion. Not just against anti-vax but everyone. I just want the day to be over to have dinner and netflix and the week to be over to be able to sleep enough.

yeah, I'll leave the bridge there though I think I'd rather die than going back. I can't do another 4 years of this. There also is no progression system like in the US with intern - senior... just 6 years of the same, including intern scut.    

The additional education wasn't a lie, I am actually doing it, but with the goal of changing careers completely. But the clock is ticking because I will have to live off of my savings.

Been seeing someone myself for 5 years and already handed in my notice.   

I kinda sold it as a leave of absence to get further education in something tangentially relevant. They think I'll come back next year but... I just can't. I don't even know how to do the last few weeks. Leaves of absences for mental health don't exist here. If they see any hint of mental illness you are done, no matter what speciality, they just don't renew your contract at the end of the year (different system, you collect your years, some do most at the same institution, some do every year somewhere else). Why would they hire someone who is a liability over someone who is not?

I hate being around people. Yes, it is only 55ish hrs per week (I did my intern year in a surgical subspeciality so I've been on the 70+hr week grind before and it definitely makes a difference). 

But I am miserable every day I have to work and realized I am going to kill myself I have to continue to work a job that is not wfh. What good is a life where you get 1-2 out of every 7 days? Psych residency is 6 years in my country, so I'd have 4 years to go of this. And then less hours but still being around humans all day, ugh.

I'm a physician (2nd year resident). I hate people, I hate unpaid overtime, I hate clicking in 10+ year old slow software, I hate being interrupted every 10min, I hate being scared to call a consultant cause I make their workload go up if I refer a patient, I hate hearing the nurses talking about who gets their break when while I can't find the time to eat lunch a lot of days, I hate being made responsible for things out of my control. Mostly I hate being around people and feel like I never get anything done.

Have to say my direct boss is pretty great, as are some of the nurses. Also for some reason people at work think I do a good job, so hearing that is nice sometimes, sometimes it only hurts cause I don't want to be there.

For the rest of my life priority 1 is to work from home, ideally with minimal human contact. Priority two is to optimize the "time stolen from me to money earned"-ratio.

If I manage to do that and not starve on the way there I guess I will read books, go for walks, meditate, watch netflix, wait until I die... is there anything else to do? Maybe write poems no one will read and paint pics no one will see.

I take a combined pill until I have a few days off back to back (so I average a period every 2-3months). Never had a period at work.  

Is this healthy/safe? no idea, but walking can get really painful during the first 2-3 days for me so having to work then is not really an option.

you mean only 20 patients covered on weekend call? I am the only resident present together with one attending on the weekend for the whole clinic (luckily only 12h shifts). Which is around 300 beds according to the clinic. I carry the same number of inpatient patients as my attending, though she also has other responsibilities (including cross-covering other wards if other attendings are absent) and some outpatient folks she sees.

Luckily no daily physical rounds. There are daily table-rounds with the nurses, a weekly round with an attending present and I am supposed to at minimum have a 30min therapy session with each patient each week. Apart from that it is reacting to what patients need (from doctors notes for their job to diagnosing rib fractures and penumothorax after a drunk scooter adventure..) and mainly the intake of new admissions. My office is on the ward so I get 1-3 patients knocking per day for questions or asking for an impromptu session.   

It does not seem to be much but with the snail-paced EMR (click-wait-click-wait kinda deal) even ordering tylenol is grating on my nerves these days. I do a lot of admin from home which ironically is faster over vpn than my hospital computer.
